fields.meta_title: Checkout Form Builder for Equipment and Keys | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a checkout form that records who has each laptop or key, when it is due back and the condition it came home in, all in one table you own.
fields.h1: Build a Checkout Form That Shows Who Has Every Item
fields.hero_description: A checkout form records who borrowed an item and the date it should come back. Emergent builds yours from a description, with a live table of everything out right now.
fields.features_subheading: A paper log shows who signed last. This checkout form keeps each loan, and its return, on one record you can search.
fields.feature_1:
Asset tags that fill in the item

Scan or type the asset tag and the form pulls the serial number and last condition from your inventory table. Nobody has to hunt for the right laptop in a long dropdown.
fields.feature_2:
A due date on every loan

Set a loan period for each type of item, such as one day for keys and three weeks for books. The form writes the due date on the record and emails the borrower before it passes.
fields.feature_3:
Condition noted at both ends

Ask for a photo and a short note when an item goes out, then again when it comes back. A cracked screen gets caught at the return desk instead of three borrowers later.
fields.feature_4:
A signature before anything leaves

Require a signature on your lending terms, from the borrower or from a parent when the borrower is a student. Until it arrives, nobody at the desk can mark the item as out.
fields.feature_5:
One table of everything that is out

Each loan becomes its own row, with the borrower and the due date. Filter the table to what is overdue, or sort it by borrower to see everything one person still has.
fields.feature_6:
Code you can take with you

Export the full codebase to your GitHub repository when IT wants the form inside the staff portal, or when a developer is ready to wire it to your asset management system.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Lending Desks, Four Sets of Rules
fields.tab_content_1:
A signature from a parent, then the Chromebook

At Ridgeway Middle School, a student scans the asset tag on a Chromebook's lid and the form fills in its serial number. The laptop stays on the cart until a parent signs the take-home agreement on their phone. The IT office opens one list each morning. Today it shows 14 students still waiting on a parent.
fields.tab_content_2:
Keys out past 6 pm and who has them

Harbor Lane Property Management lends unit keys to plumbers and cleaners for the day. Each contractor enters the key number and their company at the front desk, then signs for it. Any key still out at 6 pm sends the property manager a Slack message with the holder's company and phone number.
fields.tab_content_3:
Odometer out, odometer in, miles on the record

Millbrook's public works department runs 22 pool trucks. A driver enters the odometer reading at pickup and again at return, along with the budget the trip belongs to. Truck 14 left at 48,210 miles and came back at 48,342. The record logs 132 miles against the parks budget.
fields.tab_content_4:
A Monday list of every overdue book

The Fairhaven Community Center lends books from a shelf by the front door, each one due 21 days after checkout. Two days before that, the borrower gets an email with the title and the due date. Every Monday at 9 am, the volunteer who runs the shelf receives the titles still out past their date.

fields.howto_title: How to Build an Equipment Checkout Form
fields.howto_description: Settle what you lend and on what terms before you describe the form.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Start with the inventory you keep
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Give each type of item a loan period
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Choose what to record at return
fields.howto_step_1_des: Pull up the spreadsheet or asset list you keep today, with a tag number, model and serial for each item. Label anything that has no tag yet. Borrowers then never type a serial number, because the form looks each item up by its tag.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Decide how long each kind of item may stay out. Keys might come back the same evening while laptops stay out until the end of term. Write down what happens when something is late and who should hear about it first.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Pick the items that cannot leave the desk until someone signs your terms. A student device usually needs a parent's signature, while a stapler needs none. Mark the cost of replacing each item so the terms can state it.
fields.howto_step_4_des: List what staff check when an item comes back: a photo, a condition note, the odometer for a vehicle or missing parts for a kit. Recording the same details at both ends is what makes damage traceable to one borrower.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Put the inventory and your loan rules into one plain-English prompt. Emergent builds the checkout form and the table behind it. To change a loan period later, ask for the change in that same chat.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Connect email for due-date reminders and Slack for alerts that need a person today. Anything with an API, such as your help desk or asset management tool, can receive each loan and each return as it happens.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Book a test checkout on your phone
fields.howto_step_7_des: Check out a real item to yourself, sign for it, then return it with a photo. Confirm the due date is right and the reminder arrives. Check that the item shows as available again in the table once it is back.
